title: Spiral fallback orchestration for downstreams and tenant-aware eviction
creator: Alex Chen
description:
Background: We have recurring incidents where a single regional Redis/Kafka/DB dependency exhibits tail latency spikes or partial outage, leading to cascading request queueing and SLO violations for the Redwood text-generation API. Existing strategies (simple circuit breakers + regional failover) reduce blast radius but are too coarse: they either cut traffic too early (hurting availability) or too late (hurting latency SLOs).

Proposal (Spiral Fallback Orchestration): Implement a tenant-aware, multi-layer fallback orchestration that degrades a request surface in concentric 'rings' around the primary path. Each ring is an ordered fallback with clear timers, scoring, and per-tenant priorities. The orchestration coordinates connection-pool throttling, circuit breakers, and targeted load shedding so degradations are gradual and observable. Key ideas: spiral expansion (local->regional->fallback-cache->best-effort-stub), session-aware connection draining, token-bucket admission per-tenant, and graded response modes (full, trimmed, best-effort, stub).

Why this is different: Instead of binary failover to a secondary region, the system makes a sequence of smaller degradations that preserve SLOs for top-tier tenants while progressively protecting the platform from overload. The approach emphasizes explainable, reversible steps and integrates with rollout and canary policies.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation can route degraded requests through at least 4 fallback rings (local replica, regional replica, read-only cache, stub) with configurable timers
Per-tenant admission control prevents CPU/queue growth under sustained downstream degradation: p99 tail latency for control path <= 1200ms during simulated downstream outage
Circuit breaker thresholds and hysteresis documented and stored in config; metrics emitted for each state transition
Automated chaos test (Redis/Kafka/DB latency injection) shows system preserves 99% of successful requests for P0 tenants and limits total error budget consumption to <25% in 30m window
Rollout plan and runbook updated and reviewed by SRE and Product; new dashboards show fallback ring metrics, per-tenant shed rate, and connection pool occupancy
tasks: Write Confluence design doc describing spiral fallback states, timers, and scoring model - https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Spiral+Fallback
Prototype admission controller that uses token-buckets per-tenant and per-route
Extend connection-pool to support session-aware draining and 'soft quotas' per-tenant
Implement fallback controller that coordinates CBs, cache-prefetch, and regional reroute
Add emission of new metrics: fallback_ring, fallback_reason, cb_state, tenant_shed_ratio
Create chaos engineering tests in staging that inject tail latency and partial failures for Redis/Kafka/DB
Update runbook and add synthetic SLI tests to CI
Performance testing and cost analysis: verify batching impact under degrade modes
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable spiral fallback for 5% of traffic for internal tenants in us-west-2; monitor tail latency and consumer-facing error rates for 48h
Phase 2 (tiered): expand to 25% including a small set of P0 customers with manual rollback trigger
Phase 3 (global): enable by default with tunable per-tenant policies and automated warm-pool shadowing for cold regions
Rollback: immediate disable of fallback controller flag + gradual reconnection draining with 5s linear window

comments: 2026-03-01 Alex Chen: Created ticket after last-week incident; initial spike analysis attached to design doc.
2026-03-03 Maya Patel: Sketched admission controller API; leaning toward in-memory token-bucket with Redis fallback for lease recovery. Posted prototype outline to the design doc.

2026-03-05 SRE Review (Jordan Rivera): Concerned about cross-region redirect cost and added requirement to measure egress. Suggested adding warm-pool shadowing to reduce cold-starts. See comment in Confluence.
2026-03-06 Design Review: Agreed on 4 fallback rings and per-tenant priorities. Decided to keep CBs conservative (longer open windows) and use progressive backoff for re-open attempts.
2026-03-08 Implementation: Prototype admission controller PR opened - https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1882. Basic metrics wired (fallback_ring, cb_state).

2026-03-09 QA: Ran staging chaos test with Redis latency injection (p50=30ms, p99=2.1s). Observed P0 tenant p99 at 980ms under spiral fallback vs 2.4s baseline without fallback. Logged results to the PR.
2026-03-10 Security (Priya Singh): No encryption surface changes; recommend reviewing tenant metadata leakage risk via metrics. Marked security_review_required=false but follow-up audit recommended.
